newsitem.title: LATVIA: SALE OF LATVIAN SHIPPING CO SEEN SETTLED OCT.
newsitem.headline: SALE OF LATVIAN SHIPPING CO SEEN SETTLED OCT.

text.p: Latvia's privatisation agency said on Wednesday it hoped to have an investor in place for one of Latvia's largest shipping companies, Latvian Shipping Company, by October.
The agency said 14 companies have already expressed an interest in acquiring a stake in the company.
Raitis Kitners, in charge of the sale of the shipping company at the agency, told Reuters the first round of talks is expected to be finished by the end of March.
In the first stage, the agency will select one investor to take part in a new share issue of 25 to 35 percent in the Latvian Shipping Company.
"The investor having won the bid will have the possibility to later become the majority owner of Latvian Shipping," said Kitners. "This will be specified in an initial agreement."
Among the companies interested in acquiring a share in the Latvian Shipping Company, is Lavinia, a Liberian company, which already holds the majority of the Riga Transport Fleet.
Three other shipping companies are on the list, including Tufton Oceanic Ltd from Britain, Sea Trade from U.S. and Panama registered East Wind Transport Ltd.
Investment companies Nomura International and Hansa Investments, as well as Marsoft, a Norwegian finance corporation, are also among the bidders.
